title: Mount a tower CPU cooler the one way round its offset fins clear the tall memory
instruction: Mount the tower cooler on the processor: set it down so its copper base sits flat on the processor inside the black retention frame, then let go. On this board it fits only one way round.
context: Computer repairers and PC builders fitting a tower CPU cooler check its clearance to tall memory modules, the VRM heatsink and the graphics card, and turn it until it fits. A cooler with a square mounting pattern can go on four ways round, and some have their fin stack offset from the base so that it clears the memory slots only one way, normally with the fan blowing toward the rear exhaust; forced on another way, the cooler sits on the memory, off the processor, and cannot cool it. Here the cooler's fan and fins reach 37 mm from its base's centre on the outlet side, 18 mm on the fan side and 37 mm to either side; the robot has to read from the board which way round clears, turn the cooler to it, and set it down flat. Done by computer, ATM and office machine repairers (O*NET 49-2011.00).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A bench model of a motherboard at about half scale lies flat, its rear I/O edge away from the arms; everything except the cooler is fixed to the table. (1) Board: a green glass-epoxy circuit board 160 x 170 x 4 mm, from x 22.5 to 38.5 cm and y -8.5 to +8.5 cm. (2) Processor: a grey metal lid 38 x 38 mm standing 4 mm proud of the board, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0 (top 8 mm above the table). (3) Retention frame: four black steel bars 3 mm wide and 3 mm tall on the board round a 44 x 44 mm opening centred on the processor (top 7 mm, 1 mm below the lid). (4) Memory: two black aluminium modules on edge, each 4 mm thick (x), 70 mm long (y) and 30 mm tall above the board (top 34 mm), centred at y 0; the inner one's face is 27 mm from the processor's centre toward the arms (x 26.9 to 27.3 cm), the other 4 mm nearer the arms (x 26.1 to 26.5 cm). (5) VRM heatsink: a dark grey aluminium block 70 x 14 x 26 mm (70 mm along x) on the board, x 26.5 to 33.5 cm, y +4.6 to +6.0 cm (top 30 mm). (6) Graphics card: a black plastic block 120 x 20 x 50 mm standing in its slot, x 25.0 to 37.0 cm, y -4.6 to -6.6 cm (top 54 mm). (7) Rear I/O shield: a grey steel block 10 x 90 x 40 mm along the board's far edge, x 37.3 to 38.3 cm, y -4.5 to +4.5 cm (top 44 mm). (8) Foam pad: pink anti-static foam 80 x 80 x 10 mm on the table, centred at x 18.0 cm, y +23.5 cm. (9) Tower cooler, the one loose part, 0.25 kg, one rigid body: a copper base 34 x 34 x 6 mm; on it a copper block 20 x 20 x 14 mm (the heat pipes); on that, its lowest edge 20 mm above the base's bottom, a stack 74 mm wide and 50 mm tall made of a black fan 12 mm thick and aluminium fins 43 mm deep behind it. Along the airflow (fan to fins) the stack runs from 18 mm behind the base's centre (the fan's intake face) to 37 mm ahead of it (the fins' outlet face); across it, 37 mm to either side. Its centre of mass is 9 mm ahead of the base's centre and 43 mm above the base's bottom. It stands on its base centred on the pad (base centre at x 18.0 cm, y +23.5 cm) with its airflow along +y (fan toward the board). Seated on the lid, the stack's lowest edge is 28 mm above the table, below the tops of the memory, VRM heatsink, card and shield. With the airflow along +x (toward the rear I/O shield) the stack clears the memory, the VRM heatsink and the card by 9 mm each with the base centred, and by at least 4 mm wherever the base is inside the frame. Turned a quarter or half turn from that, the fan or fins land at least 5 mm onto the memory's top wherever the base is inside the frame, so the base cannot reach the lid. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step (in a real trial: a photo from above with the frame as the gauge, and a feeler gauge or a look from the side at the base). The 'base centre' is the centre of the cooler base's bottom face. 'At rest': the base centre and the centre of the stack's top have each moved 2 mm or less in the last 0.5 s. 'Let go': each gripper is open 0.9 or more (fingers at least 84.5 mm apart) or its finger zone is more than 10 mm from the cooler's bounding box. The scorer reads each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening from the embodiment's state; it cannot see a gripper's heading, so the 'finger zone' is every point within a radius of the segment from the finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper, the radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the current finger gap plus 8 mm, and 13.5 mm across). 'Seated': the base centre within 2 mm of the lid's top (above or below), the base tilted 2 degrees or less, all four of its bottom corners inside the frame's 44 x 44 mm opening seen from above, and the airflow (fan to fins) within 15 degrees of +x, toward the rear I/O shield. 'Upright': the cooler's up axis within 30 degrees of vertical. Score 0 if the cooler is not at rest. Otherwise: 1.0 if it is seated and both grippers have let go; 0.5 if it is seated but a gripper still holds it, or if both grippers have let go and it is upright, the right way round (airflow within 15 degrees of +x) and its base centre within 20 mm of the processor's centre horizontally, but it is not seated (tilted, raised or partly over the frame); 0.25 if both have let go and it is upright with its base centre over the board's outline, but turned another way round (for instance resting on the memory) or more than 20 mm from the processor's centre; 0 in every other case (still held and not seated, tipped over, still on the pad, on the table). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, 'let go' is taken as met. A cooler turned another way round cannot be seated: its fan or fins meet the memory before the base reaches the lid.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. A bench model, the board and cooler at about half scale (the processor lid near full size): the board, processor, frame, memory, VRM heatsink, card, I/O shield and foam pad are fixed blocks; the cooler is one rigid body of four boxes, mass spread evenly by volume, held on the lid by gravity alone (no screws, clips or paste). The fan does not run; heat is not simulated. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round.
reset_notes: Put the cooler back standing on its base on the pink foam pad, the base centred at x 18.0 cm, y +23.5 cm, its airflow along +y (fan toward the board, fins away from it). Everything else is fixed. Nothing is consumed.
